title: Absolute value of a threshold sign
statement: For every real number $r$, the threshold sign $[?]$ (equal to $1$ when $r\ge 0$ and $-1$ when $r<0$) has absolute value $1$.
replaced:
For every $r\in\mathbb R$, define $\sigma(r)=1$ when $r\ge0$ and $\sigma(r)=-1$ when $r<0$.
Then $|\sigma(r)|=1$.
